help.subtitle: How can we help you?
help.topic_hint: Select the topic below that best suits your question.
help.no_results: No answers found for your search

faq.q: What accounts do I have?
faq.a: Everyone has a personal main account. It is created for you, it is where money sent to your server ID arrives, and it cannot be closed. On top of it you can open Shared accounts for you and the people you trust, and Business accounts for your company.

faq.q: How do I open a new bank account?
faq.a: Open the Accounts tab and press Open Account, then choose Shared or Business. The opening fee is shown before you confirm and is paid from your personal main account. Business accounts usually need a bank agent's approval, and there is a limit on how many of each you can have. Offshore business accounts can only be opened in person at the desk of an offshore branch.

faq.q: Can other people use my account?
faq.a: Yes, on Shared and Business accounts you own. In the Accounts tab select the account and press Access, then add the person by their server ID. Members get only the permissions you tick, such as deposit, withdraw, transfer, invoices, cards or history. Managers get full access. Your personal main account cannot be shared.

faq.q: How do I close an account?
faq.a: Open the Accounts tab, select the account and use Close Account at the bottom of its details. Only the owner can close it. The remaining balance moves to your personal main account. You cannot close an account with active loans, card debt or a negative balance, and you must always keep at least one account.

faq.q: Can I do this at a bank branch instead?
faq.a: Yes. At a branch desk you can apply for a card, a loan or a business account in person. If a bank counter is on duty they review it on the spot, otherwise it goes to the approval queue like any request from the app. The ATM and the bank counter window are the only places where you can deposit or withdraw cash.

faq.q: How do I get a card?
faq.a: In the Cards tab press Request Card, pick the account first and then the card type: the account decides which cards are available, and some tiers need a higher clearance. Some cards are issued instantly and others need approval. Once issued, collect the physical card yourself at any branch card counter.

faq.q: How do I replace a card?
faq.a: In the Accounts tab select the account and press Replace card. The printing fee is charged to that account, and some card tiers print for free. Collect it at any branch card counter. Printing a new copy disables every older physical copy of that card.

faq.q: How do I use my card at an ATM?
faq.a: Insert the card and, the first time, choose your PIN. Only the cardholder can set it. Too many wrong PINs lock the card for a few minutes. Withdrawals count towards the card's daily limit, which you can adjust from the Cards tab.

faq.q: How do credit cards work?
faq.a: A credit card spends from its own credit line instead of your balance. Each billing cycle interest is added and a minimum payment is taken automatically from the linked account. Missed payments hurt your credit score, and after several in a row the card freezes until you pay the balance in full from the Cards tab. Cash advances at the ATM, when enabled, carry their own fee.

faq.q: Can I customize how my card looks?
faq.a: If the bank allows it, use the design option on a card in the Cards tab to set your own image link, for a small fee. Only you see custom designs, and you can turn them off in Settings › Appearance to always see the standard style.

faq.q: I lost my card, what do I do?
faq.a: Freeze it from the Cards tab: a frozen card stops working at ATMs and in shops, even if someone knows the PIN. Then order a replacement from the Accounts tab and collect it at a branch card counter. Printing it disables the lost card for good.

faq.q: Why is my account frozen?
faq.a: The bank can freeze accounts during an investigation or at your request. While frozen, no money can enter or leave the account. Visit a bank agent to resolve it.

faq.q: Why was my transfer put on hold?
faq.a: Unusually large deposits or transfers, or many in a short time, can be held for review. The money leaves your account right away and reaches the destination automatically when the review period ends, unless the bank decides to return it to you or keep it. You get an email either way.

faq.q: How do I send money to someone?
faq.a: From the Dashboard press Send and choose the source account. To pay a person, enter their server ID or pick a contact: the money always goes to their personal main account. To pay into any other account, such as a shared or business one, enter its account number, which the owner can copy from Receive.

faq.q: Are there transfer fees?
faq.a: Moving money between your own accounts is free. Transfers to someone else's account may have a small fee, shown before you confirm, and there is a daily limit on how much you can send to others.

faq.q: How do money requests work?
faq.a: Press Request on the Dashboard, choose the account that will receive the money, then enter the person's server ID or pick a contact, the amount and an optional note. They can pay or decline it from their app, and you can cancel it while it is still pending.

faq.q: How do I bill someone for my services?
faq.a: Open Invoices and create a new one. Choose who you bill as, yourself or your business if you are allowed to, enter the customer's server ID, the amount and a concept. The customer has to be near you. The money arrives when they pay.

faq.q: What happens if I don't pay an invoice?
faq.a: After a few days an unpaid invoice becomes overdue. Overdue invoices lower your credit score, and the bank may collect them automatically from money that later arrives in your accounts.

faq.q: What are saving plans?
faq.a: Saving plans set money aside for a goal, separated from your account balance so you don't spend it by accident, and they earn interest. You can add or withdraw at any time.

faq.q: What does locking a plan do?
faq.a: When you create a plan you can lock it for a fixed number of days to earn bonus interest. Withdrawing before the lock ends is allowed, but you lose the bonus interest earned so far.

faq.q: How do loans work?
faq.a: In the Loans tab choose the loan type, amount, term and the account that receives the money. Requests are usually reviewed by a bank agent, who may offer a different amount or term. Once approved, the total with interest is split into daily repayments charged automatically. Some loan types need a minimum credit score or a business account.

faq.q: What are quick loans?
faq.a: Small loans with a short term that are paid out instantly, with no review, if your credit score is high enough. They usually carry more interest than regular loans.

faq.q: What if I miss a loan payment?
faq.a: Each missed repayment adds a late fee and lowers your credit score. Too many missed repayments put the loan in default, and the bank then collects the debt automatically from money that arrives in your accounts. You can always pay repayments manually from the Loans tab.

faq.q: What is my credit score?
faq.a: A number between 300 and 850 that summarizes your banking history. The bank uses it to decide which loans and card tiers you can access. 780 or more is Excellent, 700+ is Good, 600+ is Fair and anything below is Poor.

faq.q: How is the score calculated?
faq.a: Everyone starts from 650. It rises with the money you hold across your accounts (one point per £10,000, up to +100) and with every loan you fully repay (+15 each, permanent). It falls with missed loan repayments and missed credit card payments (-20 each), overdue invoices and late vehicle financing payments (-15 each), and defaulted loans (-100 each).

faq.q: How do I improve my score?
faq.a: Keep healthy balances, make sure the accounts linked to your loans and credit cards have funds on the due date, pay invoices before they go overdue, and finish your loans: every fully repaid loan adds a permanent bonus.

faq.q: What hurts my score, and can it recover?
faq.a: Missed loan repayments and card payments stop counting once you catch up, and overdue invoices stop hurting once they are paid. A defaulted loan stays on your record permanently. A low score locks you out of some loan types, quick loans and higher card tiers.

faq.q: How do I start attending clients at the counter?
faq.a: Open the Desk tab, pick the branch you are working at and press Start shift. You need permission to approve at least one type of request. While you are on duty, requests that clients make at that branch's desk come straight to you instead of the approval queue.

faq.q: A client is waiting at the desk. What do I do?
faq.a: Their ticket appears under Clients at the desk. Press Attend to claim it: the client sees your name and you get the request together with their credit report. Approve or deny it from there. You can only attend request types you have permission for.

faq.q: What happens if nobody attends a ticket in time?
faq.a: Waiting tickets expire after a short time and the client is told to try again later. The request itself is not lost: it stays pending in the Queue tab, where any agent can still review it. A claimed ticket gets extra time while you review it.

faq.q: Why do some clients appear ahead of others in the line?
faq.a: Some card tiers include priority service as a perk. The line is ordered by priority first, then by arrival.

faq.q: What happens if I forget to end my shift?
faq.a: Your duty ends automatically when you disconnect, and any ticket you had claimed goes back to the line for another bank counter. Otherwise press End shift when you leave the counter so new desk requests go to the approval queue again.

faq.q: What lands in the approval queue?
faq.a: Every pending request: loan applications, cards that require approval and business account openings, whether they were sent from the Banking app or from a branch desk with no bank counter on duty. The sidebar shows a counter of what is pending. If the server uses automatic approvals, some requests are approved without reaching you, and requests left unreviewed for too long can be declined automatically.

faq.q: How should I review a request?
faq.a: Press Review to open the request next to the client record: credit score, score factors, accounts summary and loan history. For loans you can change the amount or the term before approving as a counter-offer. You can only review the request types you have permission for.

faq.q: Do I need to charge the client anything?
faq.a: No. Any fee, such as a card fee or the business account opening fee, is charged to the client automatically when you approve. If they don't have enough funds, the approval fails, the request stays pending and the client is told to add funds.

faq.q: Is a note required?
faq.a: A note is optional when approving and mandatory when denying, so the client always knows the reason. Notes are included in the decision email the client receives.

faq.q: How do I read the credit score?
faq.a: The score summarizes payment behavior: loans repaid, missed repayments, overdue invoices, missed credit card payments and defaults. Excellent and Good clients are low risk. Treat it as guidance, the final decision is yours.

faq.q: How exactly is the credit score calculated?
faq.a: Base 650, plus one point per £10,000 held across the client's accounts (up to +100), plus 15 per fully repaid loan. Minus 20 per missed loan repayment, 20 per missed credit card payment, 15 per overdue invoice, 15 per late vehicle financing payment and 100 per defaulted loan. Clamped between 300 and 850. Bands: 780+ Excellent, 700+ Good, 600+ Fair, below 600 Poor. Missed and overdue penalties go away once they are paid; defaults are permanent.

faq.q: How does a client receive their physical card?
faq.a: You never hand cards over. When a card is issued, whether approved by you or opened directly from the app, it is queued at the bank's card counter. The client collects it themselves at any branch card counter, and the card is linked to the account it was issued for.

faq.q: How do card replacements work?
faq.a: The client orders the replacement from the Cards page of their Banking app and pays the printing fee there; some card tiers print for free. They collect it themselves at a branch card counter, with nothing for you to do or charge. Printing a new copy disables every older physical copy of that card, which is what a client should do after losing one.

faq.q: A client cannot use their card at the ATM.
faq.a: A new card has no PIN yet: the first time it is used at an ATM, the cardholder sets it. Anyone else inserting a card without a PIN is rejected. Too many wrong PINs lock the card for a few minutes. A frozen card or a frozen account is also refused at the ATM.

faq.q: What is tier clearance?
faq.a: It is the highest card tier a client is allowed to request. By default it follows their credit score automatically. With the card approval permission you can set a fixed tier from the client record, which ignores the score until you switch it back to automatic. Higher tiers unlock better limits, fees and perks, so grant them to trusted clients.

faq.q: How do I look up a client?
faq.a: Open the Clients tab and search by name, identifier or account number, then pick the match to open their record. You need the client access permission. For privacy, balances, account numbers, cards, savings and transactions are never shown, only counts and the credit profile. Opening a record is logged.

faq.q: When should I freeze a client's accounts?
faq.a: During fraud investigations or at the client's own request. Use Freeze all accounts in the record, which needs the freeze permission. It blocks every movement on all the accounts the client owns until you release them, and the client is notified by email.

faq.q: How do I contact a client?
faq.a: From the client record you can email them their full credit report or write them a message signed by the bank. You need the email permission, and the client must have a mailbox linked to their bank profile.

faq.q: Who can manage employees?
faq.a: The boss of the banking job has every permission. Other employees only get what a boss, or someone with the manage employees permission, grants them in the Employees tab. Hiring there by server ID gives the player the banking job and firing removes it, whether they are online or not.

faq.q: I opened the terminal but most tabs are missing.
faq.a: New employees start without permissions. Ask your boss to grant them in the Employees tab; the terminal updates as soon as they save.

faq.q: Is my activity recorded?
faq.a: Yes. Approvals, denials, freezes, tier changes, client record views, emails and reports, shifts, and changes to employees are written to the activity log under your name. Bosses and anyone with the manage employees permission can review each employee's history from the Employees tab.

security.title: Security
security.subtitle: Suspicious activity on your cards and accounts.
security.none: Nothing suspicious. Your cards look fine.
security.frozen_hint: Unfreeze one from the Cards tab once you have it back.
security.step_freeze_hint: From the Cards tab. It stops working at cash machines and in shops, even if the thief knows the PIN.
security.step_replace_hint: From the Accounts tab with Replace card, then collect it at any branch card counter. The new card keeps your limit and your history.
security.step_dead_hint: Printing the replacement kills the stolen card, so whatever the thief carries opens nothing.

design.title: Card design
design.sub: Put your own image on this card. Only you see it.
design.status_format: Use a full https:// image link
design.status_broken: The image could not be loaded
design.hidden_note: Custom designs are hidden in Settings > Appearance, so the preview shows the standard design. You can still apply one.

catalog.d_cardTypes: Design, price and perks of every card the bank issues
catalog.d_loanTypes: Loan categories and who can ask for them
catalog.d_quickLoans: Instant offers paid out without a banker
catalog.d_lockPlans: Locked savings terms and their bonus rate
catalog.d_tierRules: Credit score that unlocks each card tier automatically
catalog.d_themes: Accent colours players can pick in the app
catalog.perks_hint: A player gets the perks of their best non-frozen card. Multipliers: 1 = normal, 0.5 = half, 2 = double.
catalog.id_hint: Lowercase, no spaces. Cannot change after saving.
catalog.approval_hint: Requests wait for a banker or automation.
catalog.business_only_hint: Can only be issued on business accounts.
catalog.manual_hint: Automation never approves it; a banker must.
catalog.item_hint: Physical cards need an inventory item named "{id}".

receive.server_id_note: Players nearby can also send to your main account with your server ID.

send.sub: To an account number or a nearby player ID.

request.sub: Ask someone to pay you, or split a bill.

currency.label: Currency symbol
currency.desc: Shown before every amount in the apps, mails and receipts.

accountPrefix.label: Account number prefix
accountPrefix.desc: Letters at the start of new account numbers. Existing accounts keep theirs.

businessRequiresApproval.label: Business needs approval
businessRequiresApproval.desc: Business accounts go to the banker queue instead of opening instantly.

businessAccountCost.label: Business account fee
businessAccountCost.desc: Charged when a business account request is approved.

maxBusinessAccounts.label: Max business accounts
maxBusinessAccounts.desc: How many business accounts a single player can own.

maxSharedAccounts.label: Max shared accounts
maxSharedAccounts.desc: Shared accounts a player can own or manage at the same time. Being made manager of someone else's shared account counts too.

sharedAccountCost.label: Shared account fee
sharedAccountCost.desc: Charged from personal main account when a player opens a shared account.

maxAccessPlayers.label: Max shared members
maxAccessPlayers.desc: How many players can be granted access to one account.

maxContacts.label: Max contacts
maxContacts.desc: Saved payees a player can keep.

transactionRetentionDays.label: Transaction retention
transactionRetentionDays.desc: Transactions older than this are deleted to save space. Set 0 to keep everything.

externalTransferFeePct.label: External transfer fee
externalTransferFeePct.desc: Percent charged when sending money to an account owned by someone else.

dailyTransferCap.label: Daily transfer cap
dailyTransferCap.desc: Most a player can transfer to other people's accounts per day: app, ATM, accepted money requests and standing orders combined. Card tiers multiply it. 0 = unlimited.

defaultTierClearance.label: Default card tier access
defaultTierClearance.desc: Highest card tier open to everyone. Above it, a banker must grant clearance per client.

enabled.label: Debug mode
enabled.desc: Prints every callback and money flow to the server and client consoles. Turn it on to diagnose, off on a busy server.

SchedulerIntervalMinutes.label: Scheduler interval
SchedulerIntervalMinutes.desc: Minutes between loan auto-debits, overdue checks and cleanup. Also how often stock prices move.

maxAmount.label: Max money request
maxAmount.desc: Largest amount a player can request from another player.

expireDays.label: Money request expiry
expireDays.desc: Pending requests are cancelled after this many days.

enabled.label: Recurring payments
enabled.desc: Players can schedule repeating transfers from the send flow.

maxFails.label: Failures before cancel
maxFails.desc: Missed charges before a recurring payment cancels itself.

minIntervalDays.label: Shortest interval
minIntervalDays.desc: Fewest days allowed between two charges of a recurring payment.

maxWithdraw.label: Max withdrawal
maxWithdraw.desc: Largest cash withdrawal in one go. Card tiers multiply it.

maxDeposit.label: Max deposit
maxDeposit.desc: Largest cash deposit in one go.

maxTransfer.label: Max transfer
maxTransfer.desc: Largest transfer from an ATM. Card tiers multiply it.

feePct.label: Withdrawal fee
feePct.desc: Percent charged on ATM withdrawals. Card tiers reduce it.

quickAmounts.label: Quick amounts
quickAmounts.desc: One-tap amounts shown on the withdraw and deposit screens.

maxAttempts.label: Wrong PIN attempts
maxAttempts.desc: Failed tries before the card locks.

lockMinutes.label: Card lock time
lockMinutes.desc: How long a card stays locked after too many wrong PINs.

statementRows.label: Mini statement rows
statementRows.desc: Movements printed on an ATM mini statement.

enabled.label: Cards
enabled.desc: Players can request debit and credit cards.

enabled.label: Physical cards
enabled.desc: Cards are handed out as inventory items that can be lost, given away or stolen.

defaultType.label: Default card type
defaultType.desc: Card the issueCard export hands out when the caller does not name a type.

printCost.label: Print cost
printCost.desc: Ordering a physical card from the app costs this much. The player collects it at a branch.

maxPendingOrders.label: Max pending orders
maxPendingOrders.desc: Card orders a player can have waiting at the branch.

inactivityDays.label: Inactive card expiry
inactivityDays.desc: Cards unused this long stop working on the next restart and must be replaced at the bank. 0 disables.

enabled.label: Custom card designs
enabled.desc: Card holders can put their own image on their card from a link. Only they see it.

fee.label: Design fee
fee.desc: Charged from personal main account each time a holder applies a new design. Removing it is free.

interestPct.label: Interest per cycle
interestPct.desc: Percent added to the outstanding balance at the end of every billing cycle. 0 disables interest.

cycleDays.label: Billing cycle
cycleDays.desc: Days between statements. On each one interest is charged and the minimum payment is taken from the card's account.

minPaymentPct.label: Minimum payment
minPaymentPct.desc: Percent of the outstanding balance collected automatically on each statement.

minPaymentFloor.label: Minimum payment floor
minPaymentFloor.desc: The minimum payment is never below this, unless the balance itself is smaller.

maxMissedBeforeFreeze.label: Misses before freeze
maxMissedBeforeFreeze.desc: Missed minimum payments before the card freezes itself. It unfreezes once the balance is paid in full. Every missed payment also lowers the holder's credit score.

cashAdvance.label: Cash advances
cashAdvance.desc: Credit cards can withdraw cash at the ATM against their credit line.

cashAdvanceFeePct.label: Cash advance fee
cashAdvanceFeePct.desc: Percent charged on every cash advance, on top of the amount. Replaces the regular ATM fee for credit cards.

cashAdvancePct.label: Cash share of the line
cashAdvancePct.desc: How much of the credit line can be out as cash at once. Payments free it up again.

enabled.label: Overdraft
enabled.desc: Card tiers let account owners spend below zero on their own ledger accounts, up to the tier limit.

feePct.label: Overdraft usage fee
feePct.desc: Percent charged on the newly overdrawn amount every time a movement digs deeper into the red.

dailyInterestPct.label: Overdraft daily interest
dailyInterestPct.desc: Percent of the negative balance charged once a day while the account stays in the red.

enabled.label: Loans
enabled.desc: Players can request loans from the bank.

requiresApproval.label: Loans need approval
requiresApproval.desc: Loan requests go to the banker queue instead of paying out instantly.

interestPct.label: Interest rate
interestPct.desc: Percent added on top of the borrowed amount.

termOptions.label: Loan terms
termOptions.desc: Repayment periods players can choose from.

missedPaymentFeePct.label: Missed payment fee
missedPaymentFeePct.desc: Percent of the repayment added to the debt on a missed payment.

enabled.label: Debt collection
enabled.desc: Overdue invoices and defaulted loans are collected automatically from incoming money on personal accounts and on shared accounts the debtor owns.

maxPct.label: Max garnish percent
maxPct.desc: Largest share of each incoming payment the bank may seize to settle debts.

enabled.label: Savings plans
enabled.desc: Players can create savings goals.

interestPct.label: Savings interest
interestPct.desc: Annual rate on savings plans, accrued daily. Set to 0 to disable.

minTarget.label: Min goal
minTarget.desc: Smallest target a savings plan can have.

maxTarget.label: Max goal
maxTarget.desc: Largest target a savings plan can have.

enabled.label: Invoices
enabled.desc: Players can bill each other from the app.

dueDays.label: Invoice due days
dueDays.desc: Days before an unpaid invoice is marked overdue.

minAmount.label: Min invoice
minAmount.desc: Smallest amount an invoice can bill.

maxDistance.label: Max distance
maxDistance.desc: How far away the billed player can be from the sender.

enabled.label: Stock market
enabled.desc: Players can trade shares from the Invest tab.

feePct.label: Brokerage fee
feePct.desc: Percent charged on both buying and selling. A round trip costs double this.

maxPositionValue.label: Max investment per stock
maxPositionValue.desc: Cap on what one player can hold in a single stock, valued at the current price. 0 = no cap.

dailySellCap.label: Daily sell cap
dailySellCap.desc: Most a player can cash out of the stock market per day. Card tiers multiply it. 0 = unlimited.

floorPct.label: Price floor
floorPct.desc: A stock can never fall below this percent of its base price.

ceilPct.label: Price ceiling
ceilPct.desc: A stock can never rise above this percent of its base price.

historyPoints.label: Chart points
historyPoints.desc: Price points kept per stock for the charts.

meanReversion.label: Pull to fair value
meanReversion.desc: How hard a price is dragged toward its fair value each tick. Higher is calmer and recovers faster; 0 lets prices wander until they hit a clamp.

fairReversion.label: Fair value anchor
fairReversion.desc: How hard the fair value itself returns to the listing's base price. Keep it well under the pull above, or listings drift off and never come back.

fairDrift.label: Fair value wander
fairDrift.desc: How much a stock's fair value moves on its own, as a fraction of its volatility. This is what stops 'buy anything under its base price' from being free money.

fairMin.label: Fair value floor
fairMin.desc: Lowest the fair value can wander, as a multiple of the base price.

fairMax.label: Fair value ceiling
fairMax.desc: Highest the fair value can wander, as a multiple of the base price.

trendStrength.label: Trend strength
trendStrength.desc: Largest total move a bull or bear run makes over its whole life. 0.5 = up to 50%. Not per tick.

trendMinTicks.label: Trend min length
trendMinTicks.desc: Shortest a bull/bear run can last, in scheduler ticks.

trendMaxTicks.label: Trend max length
trendMaxTicks.desc: Longest a bull/bear run can last, in scheduler ticks.

trendFlatChance.label: Flat trend chance
trendFlatChance.desc: Percent chance a new run is directionless instead of bull or bear.

marketSentiment.label: Market mood strength
marketSentiment.desc: Largest total move a market-wide mood makes over its life, applied to every listing at once. This is what makes whole-market green and red stretches.

shockChance.label: News shock chance
shockChance.desc: Percent chance per stock per tick of a sudden jump. Keep it low, this is the unforecastable part.

shockSize.label: News shock size
shockSize.desc: Largest percent a shock can move a price in one tick, up or down.

enabled.label: Wealth tax
enabled.desc: Periodically tax Los Santos account balances above the threshold. Offshore accounts are exempt.

wealthPct.label: Tax rate
wealthPct.desc: Percent collected from the balance above the threshold each cycle.

threshold.label: Tax-free threshold
threshold.desc: Balances at or below this are never taxed.

offshoreMaintenancePct.label: Offshore maintenance
offshoreMaintenancePct.desc: What the haven charges offshore accounts instead of tax. Keep it below the tax rate.

society.label: Collected into
society.desc: Society account that receives taxes and confiscated funds.

enabled.label: Anomaly detection
enabled.desc: Suspicious incoming movements are held in escrow until an admin reviews them or the hold expires.

holdHours.label: Hold duration
holdHours.desc: How long a movement stays held. If no admin resolves it in time, it releases itself.

bigDeposit.label: Big deposit threshold
bigDeposit.desc: A single cash deposit at or above this is held. 0 disables this trigger.

bigTransfer.label: Big transfer threshold
bigTransfer.desc: A single transfer to someone else's account at or above this is held. 0 disables this trigger.

windowInflow.label: Inflow window threshold
windowInflow.desc: Total money entering one account within the window below. Catches many small deposits that add up. 0 disables.

burstCount.label: Burst transaction count
burstCount.desc: This many movements on one account within the burst window flags the next one. Catches scripts and dupes. 0 disables.

foreignUseAlert.label: Alert on foreign use
foreignUseAlert.desc: Tells the card holder, in the app, by notification and by email, the first time someone else uses their card in an ATM session. The card keeps working until the ceiling below is reached.

stolenCardLimit.label: Stolen card ceiling
stolenCardLimit.desc: How much anyone other than the card holder may pull from a card in a day before it freezes itself. The move that would cross it is refused. 0 lets a thief drain the account.

stolenCardInstant.label: Panic multiplier
stolenCardInstant.desc: A single attempt at this many times the stolen card ceiling freezes the card immediately and pays out nothing. 0 disables the instant freeze.

webhook.label: Discord webhook
webhook.desc: Every new hold and every verdict is posted here. Leave empty to disable.

enabled.label: Unattended bank
enabled.desc: Lets the bank review requests itself when the rules below are met. Everything stays in the same queue, it is just decided without a player.

onlyWhenNoStaff.label: Only when no staff online
onlyWhenNoStaff.desc: Holds every automatic decision while a player with the banking job is connected. Leave off if your server has no banker job.

reviewMinutes.label: Re-check queue after
reviewMinutes.desc: Minutes before a pending request that automation could approve is picked up again by the scheduler. 0 only decides at request time.

expireHours.label: Deny stale requests after
expireHours.desc: Hours before a pending request nobody reviewed and automation cannot approve is denied. 0 leaves it pending forever.

enabled.label: Approve loans
enabled.desc: Small loans to clients with good credit are paid out without a banker.

maxAmount.label: Loan ceiling
maxAmount.desc: The most the bank lends on its own. Anything above waits for a banker. 0 disables automatic loans.

minScore.label: Loan credit score
minScore.desc: Minimum credit score for an automatic loan, on the usual 300-850 scale.

maxMissedPayments.label: Missed payments allowed
maxMissedPayments.desc: Missed repayments across the client's history before automation stops lending to them.

maxActiveLoans.label: Stop lending at
maxActiveLoans.desc: Automatic lending stops once the client already has this many active loans. At 1 they get one loan without a banker and have to ask for the next.

allowDefaulted.label: Lend after a default
allowDefaulted.desc: Lets automation lend to clients who defaulted on a loan before.

enabled.label: Approve cards
enabled.desc: Card requests are issued on credit score alone and the plastic waits at the branch counter.

minScore.label: Card credit score
minScore.desc: Minimum credit score for an automatic card. Tier clearance and the card type rules still apply on top.

enabled.label: Tier by credit score
enabled.desc: Unlocks the higher card tiers from the client's credit score when no banker has set their clearance by hand. A banker's decision always wins.

enabled.label: Approve business accounts
enabled.desc: Opens business accounts without a banker. Off by default, since opening one is usually worth the roleplay.

minScore.label: Business credit score
minScore.desc: Minimum credit score for an automatic business account.

BankingJob.label: Banking job
BankingJob.desc: Players with this job see the Banker Terminal. Bosses of the job get every permission.

UnemployedJob.label: Job after firing
UnemployedJob.desc: Job given to an employee fired from the Employees tab.

HireGrade.label: Hire grade
HireGrade.desc: Job grade given to new employees.

HireDistance.label: Hire distance
HireDistance.desc: How close the new employee must be to whoever hires them from the Banking Terminal. Stops staff from hiring people across the map. 0 disables the check.

enabled.label: Live bank counter
enabled.desc: Requests made at a counter go to the banker on duty there instead of the queue.

waitSeconds.label: Wait for a bank counter
waitSeconds.desc: How long a client waits at the counter before the request goes to the queue.

reviewSeconds.label: Review time
reviewSeconds.desc: How long a bank counter has to decide a claimed request.

requestCooldown.label: Desk request cooldown
requestCooldown.desc: Seconds a client waits between desk requests. They can still only have one pending request per type.

enabled.label: Bank mail
enabled.desc: Statements, alerts and receipts are sent through av_mail when it is running.

from.label: Sender address
from.desc: Address bank mails are sent from.

largeMovement.label: Large movement alert
largeMovement.desc: Movements at or above this send the owner an alert. 0 disables.

creditReportDays.label: Credit report every
creditReportDays.desc: Days between the automatic credit report mails. 0 disables.

enabled.label: Player webhooks
enabled.desc: Players can link their own Discord webhook to receive bank alerts.

username.label: Bot name
username.desc: Name shown on the webhook messages.

color.label: Embed colour
color.desc: Side colour of the webhook embeds.

enabled.label: Hacker API
enabled.desc: Lets hacking resources read account snapshots through the exports.

includeNative.label: Include personal accounts
includeNative.desc: Random targets can be personal main accounts, not only extra accounts.

minBalance.label: Min target balance
minBalance.desc: Random targets must hold at least this much when possible. 0 picks any account.

storage.label: Society funds
storage.desc: Where job and gang money is kept. av_banking society accounts are created by the Migrate tab; otherwise your av_laptop society functions are used.
